job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: Teacher: Today we are discussing how our country is managed. Rohan, do you think a village government works alone? Rohan: Yes, because it is their village and they make their own rules. Teacher: Actually, the village government is part of a larger system. It follows laws made by the state and national governments to ensure consistency. Priya: What about the old days with kings? Were they always cruel dictators? Teacher: Not necessarily. Some monarchs were wise and cared for their people, though they held all power. Today, we live in a democracy where we choose our leaders. Priya: Does everyone in the country get to vote? Teacher: In our democracy, we follow the principle of universal adult franchise. This means all citizens who are eighteen years or older have the right to vote, regardless of their wealth or education. It is not just about being a citizen; it is about meeting the age requirement. Rohan: So, the government is connected at all levels, and we have a say in who leads us. Teacher: Exactly. Whether it is the local panchayat or the national parliament, they work together under the same constitution to serve the people. It is a structured system where every level has a specific role to play in our daily lives.
response.summary: The government operates at local, state, and national levels, which are all interconnected. In a democracy, citizens aged eighteen and above participate in elections through universal adult franchise.
